name: Groin Hernias: Inguinal Anatomy, Lichtenstein and Laparoscopic Repairs

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / European Hernia Society Guidelines
clinicalPearls: Indirect inguinal hernia passes through deep ring lateral to inferior epigastric vessels; direct hernia bulges through Hesselbach triangle medial to vessels
Femoral hernia passes below inguinal ligament medial to femoral vein; rigid boundaries (lacunar ligament) confer a 40% strangulation risk
Lichtenstein tension-free mesh repair is the open standard; polypropylene mesh secured to inguinal ligament and conjoint tendon
Laparoscopic repairs (TAPP/TEP) cover the entire myopectineal orifice of Fruchaud, superior for bilateral or recurrent hernias
Anatomical danger zones in preperitoneal repair: Triangle of Doom (iliac vessels), Triangle of Pain (femoral branch of genitofemoral and LFCN)
reference.pathophysiology: Inguinal hernias result from patent processus vaginalis (indirect, congenital) or transversalis fascia attenuation in Hesselbach triangle (direct, acquired collagen disorder with decreased type I to type III collagen ratio). Incarceration occurs when contents cannot be reduced; strangulation occurs when tissue venous outflow and arterial inflow become compromised, resulting in ischemic bowel necrosis.
additionalInvestigations: Clinical physical examination in standing and supine positions during Valsalva
Groin ultrasound for occult or ambiguous groin swelling
Dynamic pelvic MRI or CT with Valsalva maneuver for complex or recurrent hernias
